## What this page covers

Use this page when maintaining the public **CVD mortality** dashboard after Mortality Step 6 has published an approved burden release.

The dashboard is a Quarto/Observable publication layer. It reads only approved public mortality files from the website mirror.

## Dashboard source

The maintained QMD is:

`site/surveillance/cvd/metrics/mortality/index.qmd`

The dashboard reads:

```text
site/downloads/files/metrics/mortality/burden/datasets/
  mort_burden_metrics_current.csv
  mort_monthly_reference_2015_2019.csv
```

It also reads the matching release catalogue record under:

`site/downloads/files/metrics/mortality/burden/catalogue/`

for release-date information.

The authoritative analytical copy remains under:

`outputs/public/metrics/mortality/burden/`

The QMD must never read from Step 2-5 private files or `public_ready`.

## Stable current data and dynamic timelines

The dashboard uses `mort_burden_metrics_current.csv`, not a release-stamped CSV, for its interactive views.

Available years, quarters and months are derived from the rows in that current file. Do not hard-code 2024, 2025, 2026 or another end year into the dashboard merely to extend the timeline.

The **release date** and **latest data period** are displayed separately because publication can lag the underlying observations.

## Primary and Inclusive definitions

The left-hand **Mortality definition** control allows:

- Primary only;
- Inclusive only; or
- Primary and Inclusive together.

The machine values remain:

```text
primary_clear_likely
upper_clear_likely_possible
```

The public labels are **Primary** and **Inclusive**. The dashboard must never add the two definitions together because Inclusive already contains Primary.

## Counts view

The count view follows the approved mortality publication scope.

### Monthly

Monthly public rows are restricted to:

- All CVD;
- both sexes;
- all ages; and
- monthly count.

Monthly charts use the fixed reviewed 2015-2019 reference asset. They must not calculate or display a rolling five-year monthly comparator.

### Quarterly and annual

Quarterly and annual views may show the approved CVD type, sex and age controls supported by the published rows. Five-year comparator lines are displayed only where the published metric dataset contains a usable comparator.

When both Primary and Inclusive are selected, quarterly/annual observed series share the same chart so the definitions can be compared directly.

## Distribution view

The distribution view uses the approved annual `MORT-BURDEN-002` rows.

It presents the published event-type, broad-age and sex distributions. When both mortality definitions are selected, the Primary and Inclusive charts are kept as separate full-width charts within each distribution subject so labels remain readable.

The definition label/accent colour identifies Primary versus Inclusive. Category colours identify Heart/Stroke, age group or sex and remain stable across the two definitions.

## The fixed monthly reference

`mort_monthly_reference_2015_2019.csv` is an approved analytical asset containing calendar-month minimum, maximum and mean values for 2015-2019 for both public mortality definitions.

The dashboard loads it exactly as published. It does not recalculate the reference from `mort_burden_metrics_current.csv`.

## Year-to-date: documented presentation exception

The monthly view includes one deliberately permitted presentation-derived statistic: **year-to-date count**.

Observable sums the published monthly All-CVD counts from January to the selected month only when every contributing row is:

- present;
- complete;
- unsuppressed; and
- numeric.

If any contributing month fails one of those conditions, YTD is unavailable. The dashboard never sums the remaining visible months and never reconstructs a protected month.

YTD is not written back to a dataset and is not an independently published BNR metric.

::: {.callout-warning title="Narrow exception only"}
This documented YTD sum is a publication-layer convenience. It does not establish a general pathway for calculating surveillance measures, comparators, percentages, rates or suppression decisions in Observable or Quarto.
:::

## Suppression display

The dashboard relies on the publication fields supplied by Mortality Step 6, including `suppression_status`, `display_value` and `disclosure_note`.

It must:

- preserve protected display values;
- avoid plotting unavailable protected numbers;
- never treat a protected value as zero;
- never calculate a comparator or percentage from a protected value; and
- never infer a protected value from related totals.

## Data page and downloads

The Data tab shows the published rows matching the current on-screen selection.

The full download card links to the approved current CSV/DTA, reference asset, metadata and release ZIP. These products represent the complete published release.

The **Download selected view (CSV)** action is different: the browser creates a convenience CSV containing the same selected rows and displayed values as the on-screen table. Protected values remain protected. This convenience file is not an authoritative analytical release and is not written back into `outputs/public/` or `site/downloads/`.

## Public methods links

Public interpretation belongs in the Public Methods Manual rather than in dashboard code. The main destination is:

`site/methods/measures/mortality.qmd`

with additional detail in:

`site/methods/interpretation/classifying-cvd-deaths.qmd`

When adding help/methods links to the dashboard, point users to those public pages rather than duplicating the method explanation inside the QMD.

## After a new mortality release

1. Confirm Mortality Step 6 completed with `PUBLISHED` and `Verification: PASSED`.
2. Confirm the current metric file, fixed reference asset, metadata, release ZIP and catalogue record exist in the website mirror.
3. Open the mortality dashboard locally.
4. Check Primary only, Inclusive only and both definitions.
5. Check monthly, quarterly and annual count views.
6. Check the annual distribution view.
7. Check data coverage, release date/latest period and the Data tab.
8. Confirm protected values remain protected.
9. Check all download links.
10. Run a complete Quarto render and inspect Git changes before deployment.

A normal new release should extend the available timeline automatically and should not require a dashboard-source edit.

## If the dashboard fails

- If the published current file is wrong or missing, return to the mortality analytical/publication workflow.
- If the published data are correct but Observable reports an error, correct the dashboard source and rerender.
- If a control offers a stratum absent from the published data, correct the publication-layer filtering rather than manufacturing a value.
- If a protected value appears to be recoverable, stop publication and investigate before deployment.

See [Update website content](update-content.qmd), [CVD mortality workflow](../workflows/mortality/overview.qmd) and [Apply and review disclosure control](../controls/disclosure-control.qmd).
